newsitem.title: FRANCE: KLM plans to up ex-Paris cargo rates in Q1.
newsitem.headline: KLM plans to up ex-Paris cargo rates in Q1.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said it plans to increase ex-Paris rates in the first quarter of next year.

"It's hard to give precise details at present but ex-Paris increases of between ten to 12 percent, effective spring 1997, are probably not far off the mark, " a Charles-de-Gaule-based KLM cargo official told Reuters.
"Over the past three to four months, we've been utilising cargo capacity more or less to the full on routes to the Far East, North America and South America, the official said.

In the current pre-Christmas/New Year rush, KLM's Paris cargo office was having to turn down between half to two-thirds of the global requests it received from customers desperate to ship out cargo before December 31, the official added.
All the main long-haul destinations were generating buoyant demand including China, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, Malaysia and Indonesia and on North Atlantic routes, Chicago and Los Angeles.

"It's a simple case of demand outstripping capacity and while this is a traditional feature at this time of year it appears to be a little stronger than the end of 1995 and this all augurs well for the market in 1997." --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
